messages:
maria: quick heads-up — pushed a short perf run on the host path. Seeing a 12-18% CPU uplift on small streaming requests after the last kernel-selector change. mostly in HTTP/2 frame handling + tokenization.
rahul: ugh. is that from the new kernel pref for small batch sizes? did you capture a flamegraph?
maria: yes. flame attached in gist but key bits: host syscall time up in grpc/hpack decode, and our tokenization is doing lots of small allocations on each frame. sample:

  34.2%  runtime  [.] decode_http2_frame
  18.7%  tokenize_host  [.] tokenize_chunk
  12.1%  kv_cache     [.] eviction_hotpath

jamie: can you paste the exact trace lines? i want to confirm it's WS->userland copy vs parse CPU.
maria: pasted logs below (trimmed):

  2026-03-20T14:12:03Z host1 grpc: read 128 bytes -> hpack decode (allocs=18)
  2026-03-20T14:12:03Z host1 tokenize: fragment size 32 -> new buffer -> utf8-normalize

maria: two theory bullets: (1) kernel selector bumped to prefer small-batch kernels which reduce decode time in the GPU path but increase host preparse because we now get many tiny frames; (2) KV cache policy thrashes when fragments <64 bytes because keys aren't canonicalized before lookup, causing eviction churn.
leo: interesting — so optimization traded host parse for model kernel latency. we need a win-win. can we coalesce small frames on the edge before tokenize? that would reduce syscall & allocation count.
rahul: reminded of the preparse shim we prototyped last month. if we add a lightweight coalescer between ingress and tokenizer that buffers up to N ms or M bytes, we might avoid small-frame penalty without changing kernel preferences.
jamie: agree. also we should tweak KV lookup to use a stable hash of canonicalized prefix (2-4 bytes) to avoid micro-evictions for tiny fragments. cheap compute, big payback.
maria: patched a minimal PoC: in Rust proxy we add a tiny ring buffer. behavior: buffer until either total_bytes >= 256 or time >= 6ms then forward combined frame. microbench results:

  before: host CPU per-request 6.2ms, allocs 18
  after: host CPU per-request 4.1ms, allocs 4

maria: pushed to staging as canary. infra-bot: deploy staging/proxy-coalesce/sha=cb9a2 now
infra-bot: deploy staging/proxy-coalesce/sha=cb9a2 started by maria at 2026-03-20T14:18:12Z
leo: can we also flip kernel selector back in the canary to previous threshold and run e2e p99 latency? need both sides.
rahul: i'll roll the kernel selector flag in the canary (kselector.small_batch_threshold=48->96) and enable the coalescer. running perf harness now.
rahul: quick results from harness (1000 reqs, mixed lengths):

  p50 latency: baseline 32ms -> canary 30ms
  p95 latency: baseline 120ms -> canary 98ms
  host CPU mean: baseline 6.2ms -> canary 3.9ms
  KV eviction rate: baseline 72/min -> canary 9/min

jamie: nice. KV drop is huge — canonicalizing keys + coalesce looks effective.
maria: follow-ups: (1) add canonicalization for key lookup in kvcache codepath (cheap prefix hash), (2) land coalescer in proxy with a config toggle + telemetry (coalesce_rate, coalesced_bytes), (3) update kernel selector doc to mention host parse tradeoffs.
leo: also add an observability dashboard: tokenization allocs, http2 frame count per request, coalesce hit rate, kvcache eviction. include an alarm if coalesce hit rate < 5% for 5m (means not doing work and maybe misconfigured).
jamie: i'll own the kvcache prefix hash PR. plan to bump canary to prod after 24h and no regressions.

maria: filing a short postmortem note in #postmortems after we confirm prod numbers. thanks team :thumbsup:
